source.text: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ אֶ֚ל כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הַיֹּשְׁבִ֤ים בְּמִגְדֹּל֙ וּבְתַחְפַּנְחֵ֣ס וּבְנֹ֔ף וּבְאֶ֥רֶץ פַּתְר֖וֹס לֵאמֹֽר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: The word that came to Jeremiah for all the Judeans, the [ones] dwelling in [the] land of Egypt, the [ones] dwelling in Migdol and in Tahpanhes and in Memphis and in [the] land of Pathros, saying:

en.L: The word that came to Jeremiah for all the Judeans who were living in the land of Egypt, who were living in Migdol and in Tahpanhes and in Memphis and in the land of Pathros, saying:
en.B: This message came to Jeremiah for all the Judeans living in the land of Egypt, at Migdol, Tahpanhes and Memphis, and in the land of Pathros:
en.R: This is the message that came to Jeremiah for all the people of Judah living in Egypt, in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes and Memphis, and in the region of Pathros in southern Egypt:

decisions.choice: Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis and Pathros: places in Egypt from the northeastern border to the far south
decisions.reason: Migdol ("tower") and Tahpanhes were border fortresses on the eastern edge of the Nile delta (Exodus 14:2; 43:7-9). Memphis, called *Noph* in Hebrew, was the old capital of Lower Egypt, near the head of the delta (2:16; Isaiah 19:13). Pathros is southern or Upper Egypt, the Nile valley south of Memphis (Isaiah 11:11). By the time of this message, people from Judah had settled throughout the country.

decisions.choice: Judeans: people from Judah
decisions.reason: The word names people belonging to Judah, the kingdom and its tribe. In time it becomes the ordinary word for Jews; here it means the refugees and settlers from Judah living in Egypt.

decisions.choice: for all the Judeans: a message concerning them and addressed to them
decisions.reason: The word is for them and about them. Verses 15-19 show it was spoken to a gathering of them, and verse 24 has Jeremiah address them directly.

decisions.choice: Memphis for *Noph* at every level, as 2:16; Pathros (L, B), the region of Pathros in southern Egypt (R); Judeans (L, B), people of Judah (R)
decisions.reason: The city is given its familiar name, as at 2:16 and Isaiah 19:13. Readable says where Pathros was (m1) and says "people of Judah" for Judeans, as Readable does elsewhere. The heading follows the wording set for Jeremiah ("This message came to Jeremiah" at Balanced), without "from the LORD", which the Hebrew lacks here.

source.text: כֹּה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתֶּ֣ם רְאִיתֶ֗ם אֵ֤ת כָּל־הָֽרָעָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֵבֵ֨אתִי֙ עַל־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְעַ֖ל כָּל־עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וְהִנָּ֤ם חָרְבָּה֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין בָּהֶ֖ם יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: you, you have seen all the disaster which I brought on Jerusalem and on all [the] cities of Judah; and look, they [are] a ruin the day this, and there is not in them an inhabitant,

en.L: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: You yourselves have seen all the disaster that I brought on Jerusalem and on all the cities of Judah; and look, they are a ruin this day, and there is no inhabitant in them,
en.B: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: You have seen for yourselves all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the towns of Judah. Today they lie in ruins, and no one lives in them,
en.R: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You saw with your own eyes the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the towns of Judah. Today they are in ruins, and no one lives there.

decisions.choice: you yourselves have seen: they were witnesses of what happened
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out before the verb for emphasis. Those now in Egypt had lived through the fall of Jerusalem (39:1-10) and could not claim not to know what idolatry had cost.

decisions.choice: disaster: the same word as "evil" in verse 3
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers both wrongdoing and the harm that follows it. The people's evil (verse 3) brought on them the evil of ruin; the word runs through the chapter (verses 7, 11, 17, 23, 27, 29).

decisions.choice: the sentence continues: verse 3 gives the reason for the ruin
decisions.reason: The verse ends without completing the thought; verse 3 begins "because of their evil".

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD of hosts (L); The LORD of Armies says this (B); This is what the LORD of Armies says (R); the speech opens here
decisions.reason: The formulas set for the prophets. God's message, given through Jeremiah, runs from here to the end of verse 14 and is set in quotation marks, as Jeremiah's prose chapters quote speech (34:2; 35:13).

decisions.choice: towns (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 7:17, the word covers settlements of any size, and most in Judah were small.

source.text: מִפְּנֵ֣י רָעָתָ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ לְהַכְעִסֵ֔נִי לָלֶ֣כֶת לְקַטֵּ֔ר לַעֲבֹ֖ד לֵאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יְדָע֔וּם הֵ֖מָּה אַתֶּ֥ם וַאֲבֹתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: because of their evil which they did to provoke me, by going to burn incense to serve gods other which not they knew them, they, you and your fathers.

en.L: because of their evil that they did to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, going to burn incense [and] to serve other gods whom they had not known, they, you and your fathers.
en.B: because of the evil they did to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger. They went and burned incense and served other gods that neither they nor you nor your ancestors had ever known.
en.R: It happened because of the evil they did to make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry. They went and burned incense to other gods and served them. Neither they nor you nor your ancestors had ever known these gods.

decisions.choice: burn incense: make offerings go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to make smoke rise, and it is used both of burning incense and of burning offerings on an altar (see 19:4). It is the key word of this chapter (verses 5, 8, 15, 17-19, 21, 23, 25): the worship the people refuse to give up.

decisions.choice: they, you and your fathers: those who had not known these gods
alternatives: they, you and your fathers did this evil
decisions.reason: The three words go with "whom they had not known", as in 19:4: the gods were strangers to the people of Jerusalem, to their hearers in Egypt and to their ancestors alike. They could also be read as naming who did the evil, but the order of the sentence favors the first reading.

decisions.choice: gods they had not known: gods with no history with them
decisions.reason: Israel knew the LORD by what he had done for them; these gods had done nothing (7:9; Deuteronomy 32:17).

decisions.choice: to anger (B); make me angry (R); It happened (R)
decisions.reason: The verb "provoke" means to stir to anger, and Balanced and Readable say so. Readable starts a new sentence and says what the reason is for.

source.text: וָאֶשְׁלַ֤ח אֲלֵיכֶם֙ אֶת־כָּל־עֲבָדַ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים הַשְׁכֵּ֥ים וְשָׁלֹ֖חַ לֵאמֹ֑ר אַל־נָ֣א תַעֲשׂ֗וּ אֵ֛ת דְּבַֽר־הַתֹּעֵבָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׂנֵֽאתִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending, saying, do not please do the thing of the abomination this which I hate.

en.L: And I sent to you all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets, rising early and sending [them], saying, 'Oh, do not do this abominable thing that I hate!'
en.B: Again and again I sent you all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets to say, 'Please do not do this detestable thing that I hate!'
en.R: Over and over I sent {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets to you. They said, 'Please do not do this disgusting thing that I hate!'

decisions.choice: rising early and sending: sending prophets constantly, without giving up
abomination: something loathsome to God
decisions.reason: The word names what God finds detestable, above all the worship of other gods (Deuteronomy 7:25-26; 2 Kings 21:2). Here "this abominable thing" is the burning of incense to other gods.

decisions.choice: please: God pleads with his people
decisions.reason: The small word added to the command makes it an appeal. God does not only forbid; he begs them to stop.

decisions.choice: rising early and sending [them] (L); again and again (B); over and over (R); servants (all levels)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase in Jeremiah, and "servants" for the prophets as those who serve God (7:25).

decisions.choice: abominable thing (L); detestable thing (B); disgusting thing (R)
decisions.reason: Each level gives the strong word in its own register; Readable uses an everyday word.

source.text: וְלֹ֤א שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ וְלֹא־הִטּ֣וּ אֶת־אָזְנָ֔ם לָשׁ֖וּב מֵרָֽעָתָ֑ם לְבִלְתִּ֥י קַטֵּ֖ר לֵאלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And not they listened and not they inclined their ear to turn from their evil, so as not to burn incense to gods other.

en.L: But they did not listen, and they did not incline their ear to turn from their evil, so as not to burn incense to other gods.
en.B: But they did not listen or pay attention. They would not turn from their evil and stop burning incense to other gods.
en.R: But they would not listen or pay attention. They would not turn away from their evil ways and stop burning incense to other gods.

decisions.choice: incline their ear: bend toward to listen, pay attention
decisions.reason: As in 35:15, to turn the ear toward someone is to listen with care.

decisions.choice: to turn from their evil ... so as not to burn incense: turning meant giving up the incense
decisions.reason: The second phrase says what turning from their evil would have meant in practice: no more offerings to other gods.

decisions.choice: stop burning incense (B, R); evil ways (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the phrase "so as not to burn" asks.

source.text: וַתִּתַּ֤ךְ חֲמָתִי֙ וְאַפִּ֔י וַתִּבְעַר֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וּבְחֻצ֖וֹת יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַתִּהְיֶ֛ינָה לְחָרְבָּ֥ה לִשְׁמָמָ֖ה כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And poured out my wrath and my anger, and it burned in [the] cities of Judah and in [the] streets of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin, a desolation, as the day this.

en.L: So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger poured out and burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin [and] a desolation, as [it is] this day.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger poured out and blazed in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, and they became the ruined wasteland they are today.
en.R: So {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury and anger poured out and burned like fire in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. They became an empty ruin, as they are today.

decisions.choice: poured out ... burned: God's anger pictured as molten metal and fire
decisions.reason: The verb "pour out" is used of metal melting and flowing (Ezekiel 22:22). The same words describe God's anger in 7:20 and 42:18, the warning given before the people went to Egypt.

decisions.choice: a ruin and a desolation: places laid waste and left empty
decisions.reason: The two words together stress how complete the destruction was. The second names a deserted place that stuns those who see it.

decisions.choice: as it is this day: the ruin is still there to see
decisions.reason: The phrase points the hearers to what is true now, as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: the ruined wasteland (B); burned like fire, an empty ruin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two nouns into one phrase; Readable says that the anger burned like fire and that the ruin is empty.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לָמָה֩ אַתֶּ֨ם עֹשִׂ֜ים רָעָ֤ה גְדוֹלָה֙ אֶל־נַפְשֹׁ֣תֵכֶ֔ם לְהַכְרִ֨ית לָכֶ֧ם אִישׁ־וְאִשָּׁ֛ה עוֹלֵ֥ל וְיוֹנֵ֖ק מִתּ֣וֹךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה לְבִלְתִּ֛י הוֹתִ֥יר לָכֶ֖ם שְׁאֵרִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And now thus says Yahweh, God of hosts, God of Israel: why you [are] doing harm great to yourselves, to cut off for you man and woman, child and infant from [the] midst of Judah, so as not to leave for you a remnant,

en.L: And now thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of hosts, the God of Israel: Why are you doing great harm to yourselves, to cut off from yourselves man and woman, child and nursing infant, from the midst of Judah, so as to leave yourselves no remnant,
en.B: So now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Why are you bringing such great harm on yourselves? You are cutting off man and woman, child and infant, from among Judah, and leaving yourselves no remnant,
en.R: Now this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Why are you hurting yourselves so badly? You will cause men and women, children and babies to be cut off from Judah. None of your people will be left.

decisions.choice: why ...?: a question that warns
decisions.reason: The question does not ask for information. It shows the people that their worship is harming no one but themselves.

decisions.choice: great harm to yourselves: harm to your own lives
decisions.reason: The word for "yourselves" is the word for life or self. The harm is the same "disaster" as in verse 2; now they are bringing it on themselves.

decisions.choice: child and nursing infant: the youngest, so that no one is spared
decisions.reason: The two words name small children and babies still at the breast (Lamentations 2:11; 1 Samuel 15:3). With "man and woman" they mean the whole community.

decisions.choice: remnant: the survivors of Judah's fall
decisions.reason: After Jerusalem fell, those left in the land were the remnant (40:11, 15; 42:2). By their idolatry in Egypt they put even this last part of the people at risk.

decisions.choice: the LORD, the God of hosts (L); the LORD God of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew says "the LORD, God of hosts", as in 35:17, and the wording follows it there.

decisions.choice: You will cause ... to be cut off ... None of your people will be left.
decisions.reason: Readable divides the long question into a question and two statements.

source.text: לְהַכְעִסֵ֨נִי֙ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֣י יְדֵיכֶ֔ם לְקַטֵּ֞ר לֵאלֹהִ֤ים אֲחֵרִים֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֥ם בָּאִ֖ים לָג֣וּר שָׁ֑ם לְמַ֨עַן֙ הַכְרִ֣ית לָכֶ֔ם וּלְמַ֤עַן הֱיֽוֹתְכֶם֙ לִקְלָלָ֣ה וּלְחֶרְפָּ֔ה בְּכֹ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: by provoking me with [the] works of your hands, by burning incense to gods other in [the] land of Egypt where you [are] coming to sojourn there, so as to cut off yourselves, and so as your being for a curse and for a reproach among all [the] nations of the earth?

en.L: by provoking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with the works of your hands, by burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have come to sojourn, so as to cut yourselves off, and so as to become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
en.B: by provoking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger with what your hands have made, burning incense to other gods in Egypt, the land you have come to live in? It will only cut you off and make you a curse and a disgrace among all the nations of the earth.
en.R: You make {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry by worshiping idols you made with your own hands. You burn incense to other gods here in Egypt, where you have come to live. You will destroy yourselves. People in every nation on earth will use your name as a curse and insult you.

decisions.choice: the works of your hands: idols
decisions.reason: As in 1:16, what their hands have made are images of gods (Isaiah 2:8).

decisions.choice: sojourn: live as outsiders in a land not one's own
decisions.reason: The verb is used of living somewhere as a resident foreigner, often for a time. The people said they would go to Egypt to sojourn there (42:15, 17; 43:2).

decisions.choice: so as to cut yourselves off ... become a curse: the result of what they do
decisions.reason: They do not mean to destroy themselves, but that is where their worship leads (compare 7:18-19).

decisions.choice: a curse and a reproach: the covenant warnings come true
decisions.reason: Moses warned that Israel would become a byword among the nations (Deuteronomy 28:37), and Jeremiah repeats the warning (24:9; 42:18). To become a curse is for one's name to be used when people curse (24:9; 29:22).

decisions.choice: sojourn (L), live (B, R); curse; reproach (L), disgrace (B); Readable in sentences
decisions.reason: "Reproach" and "disgrace" follow 24:9. Readable explains the nouns in sentences of its own.

decisions.choice: It will only cut you off
decisions.reason: Balanced ends the question after the place and gives the result as a statement.

source.text: הַֽשְׁכַחְתֶּם֩ אֶת־רָע֨וֹת אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֜ם וְאֶת־רָע֣וֹת׀מַלְכֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה וְאֵת֙ רָע֣וֹת נָשָׁ֔יו וְאֵת֙ רָעֹ֣תֵכֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת רָעֹ֣ת נְשֵׁיכֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֔ה וּבְחֻצ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers and the evils of [the] kings of Judah and the evils of his wives and your evils and the evils of your wives, which they did in [the] land of Judah and in [the] streets of Jerusalem?

en.L: Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers, and the evils of the kings of Judah, and the evils of his wives, and your [own] evils, and the evils of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
en.B: Have you forgotten the wicked deeds of your ancestors, of the kings of Judah and their wives, your own wicked deeds and those of your wives, which were done in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
en.R: Have you forgotten all the evil things done in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? Your ancestors did them. The kings of Judah and their wives did them. You and your wives did them too.

decisions.choice: evils ... evils ... evils: the same word five times
decisions.reason: The repeated word piles up the guilt of every generation and group, from ancestors and kings to the hearers themselves.

decisions.choice: his wives: the wives of each of the kings
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "his wives", meaning the wives of each king of Judah. The Greek translation reads "your officials" in its place (from general knowledge). The Hebrew is followed: the wives fit the chapter, where the women's worship is at issue (verses 15, 19, 25).

decisions.choice: the kings' wives and other gods
decisions.reason: Foreign wives led kings into idolatry: Solomon's wives (1 Kings 11:4-8), Jezebel (1 Kings 16:31), and the queen mother Maacah (1 Kings 15:13).

decisions.choice: their wives (B, R)
decisions.reason: English says "their wives" after "the kings"; the sense is the same (m2).

decisions.choice: the places first, then the people in short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable puts the question first and lists who did these things in three short sentences.

source.text: לֹ֣א דֻכְּא֔וּ עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְלֹ֣א יָרְא֗וּ וְלֹֽא־הָלְכ֤וּ בְתֽוֹרָתִי֙ וּבְחֻקֹּתַ֔י אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥תִּי לִפְנֵיכֶ֖ם וְלִפְנֵ֥י אֲבוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not they have been crushed until the day this, and not they have feared, and not they have walked in my law and in my statutes which I set before you and before your fathers.

en.L: They have not been humbled to this day, and they have not feared, and they have not walked in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes that I set before you and before your fathers.
en.B: To this day they have not been humbled, and they have shown no fear. They have not lived by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, which I set before you and your ancestors.
en.R: To this day they are not sorry for what they did, and they have no fear of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching and the laws I gave to you and your ancestors.

decisions.choice: humbled: crushed in spirit, brought to repentance
decisions.reason: The verb means "crushed". Used of the heart it means broken and humble before God (Isaiah 57:15; Psalm 51:19). Even the ruin of their land has not brought them to that.

decisions.choice: they: the people are spoken about, not to
decisions.reason: God turns from "you" to "they" and back to "you". He speaks of the people as if passing judgment on them.

decisions.choice: instruction and statutes: God's teaching and his fixed laws
decisions.reason: *Torah* is God's instruction, and the second word names laws laid down for good. To walk in them is to live by them.

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B), teaching (R); statutes (L, B), laws (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for these terms (Isaiah; Numbers to Ruth).

decisions.choice: not sorry; fear of me
decisions.reason: Readable says what being humbled means here, and whom they should have feared.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֨י שָׂ֥ם פָּנַ֛י בָּכֶ֖ם לְרָעָ֑ה וּלְהַכְרִ֖ית אֶת־כָּל־יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: look, I [am] setting my face against you for harm, and to cut off all Judah.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am setting {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against you for harm, and to cut off all Judah.
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: I am setting {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face against you to bring harm, to cut off all Judah.
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I have turned against you, and I will bring disaster on you. I will cut off all of Judah.

decisions.choice: set my face against you: turn against you with fixed purpose
decisions.reason: To set one's face is to be determined; set "against" someone it means settled hostility (21:10; Leviticus 20:3-6). Verse 12 uses the same words of the people, who "set their faces" to go to Egypt: their resolve is met by God's.

decisions.choice: all Judah: all the people of Judah who went to Egypt
decisions.reason: As verse 12 shows, the threat is against the remnant in Egypt, not against the exiles in Babylon, to whom God has promised a future (24:5-7; 29:10-14).

decisions.choice: I have turned against you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom (m1).

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD of hosts (L); The LORD of Armies says this (B); This is what the LORD of Armies says (R)
decisions.reason: The formulas set for the prophets.

source.text: וְלָקַחְתִּ֞י אֶת־שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֨מוּ פְנֵיהֶ֜ם לָב֣וֹא אֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַיִם֮ לָג֣וּר שָׁם֒ וְתַ֨מּוּ כֹ֜ל בְּאֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֣יִם יִפֹּ֗לוּ בַּחֶ֤רֶב בָּֽרָעָב֙ יִתַּ֔מּוּ מִקָּטֹן֙ וְעַד־גָּד֔וֹל בַּחֶ֥רֶב וּבָרָעָ֖ב יָמֻ֑תוּ וְהָיוּ֙ לְאָלָ֣ה לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וְלִקְלָלָ֖ה וּלְחֶרְפָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will take [the] remnant of Judah who set their faces to go [to the] land of Egypt to sojourn there, and they will be finished all in [the] land of Egypt; they will fall by the sword, by the famine they will be finished, from small and to great; by the sword and by the famine they will die; and they will become an oath, a horror, and a curse and a reproach.

en.L: And I will take the remnant of Judah who set their faces to go to the land of Egypt to sojourn there, and they will all come to an end in the land of Egypt; they will fall by the sword; by famine they will come to an end, from the least to the greatest; by the sword and by famine they will die. And they will become an execration, a horror, a curse and a reproach.
en.B: I will take away the remnant of Judah who were determined to go to the land of Egypt to live there, and they will all perish in the land of Egypt. They will fall by the sword or perish by famine; least and greatest alike will die by sword and famine. They will become a name used in curses, a horror, a curse and a disgrace.
en.R: I will take away the people left from Judah who made up their minds to go and live in Egypt. They will all die there. They will be killed in war or die of famine. Everyone, from the least important to the most important, will die in war or of famine. People will use their name when they curse someone. They will be horrified at them, curse them and insult them.

decisions.choice: set their faces to go: were determined to go
decisions.reason: As in verse 11 and 42:15, 17. They chose Egypt against the word of the LORD (42:19-22; 43:2-4).

decisions.choice: come to an end: be finished off, perish
decisions.reason: The verb means to be complete, used up. It returns in verses 18 and 27, and the women use it of themselves in verse 18.

decisions.choice: an execration: a name used in oaths of cursing
decisions.reason: The word is an oath that calls down a curse on oneself or on another if it is broken (Numbers 5:21). People will name the fate of these refugees when they swear: "may I be like them if ..." (compare 29:22).

decisions.choice: an execration, a horror, a curse and a reproach: the warning of 42:18 carried out
decisions.reason: The same four words were spoken in 42:18 as a warning before the people went to Egypt. What was a warning there is now a sentence.

decisions.choice: an execration (L), a name used in curses (B); horror; curse; reproach (L), disgrace (B); Readable in sentences, as 42:18
decisions.reason: "Horror" and "curse" follow the wording set for these lists in Jeremiah, and "reproach" and "disgrace" follow 24:9. The first word is worded as in 42:18, as set for these lists: "execration" at Literal and "a name used in curses" at Balanced, so that it is not read as a promise. Readable says what each word means in sentences of its own, as it does in 42:18.

decisions.choice: sword (B), war (R); famine
decisions.reason: The pair follows the wording set for "sword, famine and pestilence" in Jeremiah.

source.text: וּפָקַדְתִּ֗י עַ֤ל הַיּֽוֹשְׁבִים֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּקַ֖דְתִּי עַל־יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בַּחֶ֥רֶב בָּרָעָ֖ב וּבַדָּֽבֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will visit on those dwelling in [the] land of Egypt as I visited on Jerusalem, with the sword, with the famine and with the pestilence.

en.L: And I will punish those who dwell in the land of Egypt as I punished Jerusalem, with the sword, with famine and with pestilence.
en.B: Those who live in the land of Egypt I will punish as I punished Jerusalem, with sword, famine and plague.
en.R: I will punish those who live in Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem, with war, famine and disease.

decisions.choice: punish: the verb "visit" used of judgment
decisions.reason: The verb means to attend to or deal with someone. With "on" it means to bring someone's deeds back on them, to punish (9:24; 11:22).

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence: the disasters of war and siege
as I punished Jerusalem: Egypt is no refuge
decisions.reason: They went to Egypt to escape war and hunger (42:14). The same three disasters will find them there (42:16-17).

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence (L); sword, famine and plague (B); war, famine and disease (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this list in Jeremiah.

records.literal_gloss: And not will there be an escapee or survivor for [the] remnant of Judah who have come to sojourn there in [the] land of Egypt, and to return [to the] land of Judah, where they [are] lifting up their soul to return to dwell there; for not they will return, except fugitives.

en.L: And there will be no escapee or survivor for the remnant of Judah who have come to sojourn there in the land of Egypt, to return to the land of Judah, to which they long to return to dwell there; for they will not return, except [some] fugitives."
en.B: Of the remnant of Judah who have come to live in the land of Egypt, none will escape or survive to go back to the land of Judah, though they long to return and live there. None will return except a few fugitives."
en.R: Of all the people from Judah who are left and have come to live in Egypt, no one will escape or survive. No one will go back to the land of Judah, though they long to return and live there. Only a few who escape will return."

decisions.choice: lift up their soul: long for, set their desire on
decisions.reason: The idiom means to yearn for something (22:27; Deuteronomy 24:15). They still hope to go home to Judah.

decisions.choice: except fugitives: a very few, not none at all
decisions.reason: The closing words soften "no escapee or survivor": a handful will get away, as verse 28 says ("few in number").

decisions.choice: no escapee or survivor: the way home closed by their own choice
decisions.reason: They went to Egypt to survive, but they will not escape there. The words echo 42:17, the warning they ignored.

decisions.choice: [some] (L); a few (B, R); speech closes
decisions.reason: "Fugitives" without "the" means only some; the levels say so (m2). God's message, opened in verse 2, closes here.

source.text: וַיַּעֲנ֣וּ אֶֽת־יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ כָּל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֤ים הַיֹּֽדְעִים֙ כִּֽי־מְקַטְּר֤וֹת נְשֵׁיהֶם֙ לֵאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְכָל־הַנָּשִׁ֥ים הָעֹמְד֖וֹת קָהָ֣ל גָּד֑וֹל וְכָל־הָעָ֛ם הַיֹּשְׁבִ֥ים בְּאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּפַתְר֥וֹס לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And answered Jeremiah all the men who knew that burning incense [were] their wives to gods other, and all the women standing [by], a great assembly, and all the people dwelling in [the] land of Egypt in Pathros, saying:

en.L: Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women who were standing by, a great assembly, and all the people who were living in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying:
en.B: Then a great assembly answered Jeremiah: all the men who were aware that their wives burned incense to other gods, all the women standing by, and all the people living in Pathros in the land of Egypt. They said:
en.R: Then a large gathering of people answered Jeremiah. In it were all the men who knew about their wives burning incense to other gods, and all the women standing there. All the people who lived in Pathros in southern Egypt were there too. They said:

decisions.choice: the men who knew: husbands who knew and allowed their wives' worship
decisions.reason: The men are named by what they knew: they were aware of the offerings and did not stop them. The women say so in verse 19.

decisions.choice: a great assembly: a large gathering of the community
decisions.reason: The word names people gathered together, often for worship. Here it may describe a crowd, or an occasion such as a festival; the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: in Pathros: where this gathering took place
decisions.reason: The words seem to place the scene in southern Egypt, though verse 1 speaks to Judeans across the whole country. They may also mean that those of Pathros were among the crowd.

decisions.choice: assembly (L, B), gathering (R); Pathros (L, B), Pathros in southern Egypt (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *qahal*; Readable says where Pathros was, as in verse 1.

decisions.choice: the crowd first, then who was in it (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say first that a great crowd answered and then list who was in it.

source.text: הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֥רְתָּ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה אֵינֶ֥נּוּ שֹׁמְעִ֖ים אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: The word which you have spoken to us in [the] name of Yahweh, not we [are] listening to you.

en.L: "[As for] the word that you have spoken to us in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, we are not listening to you.
en.B: "That message you spoke to us in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: we are not going to listen to you.
en.R: "We will not listen to the message you have given us in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the word ... first: a blunt refusal
decisions.reason: The message is named first and then dismissed: whatever Jeremiah has said, they will not listen.

decisions.choice: in the name of the LORD: speaking with the LORD's authority
decisions.reason: They do not deny that he spoke in the LORD's name. They refuse to obey all the same.

decisions.choice: [As for] (L); That message ...: (B); Readable in plain order; the speech opens
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the message first, as the Hebrew does; Readable uses ordinary order. The people's reply runs to the end of verse 18.

source.text: כִּ֩י עָשֹׂ֨ה נַעֲשֶׂ֜ה אֶֽת־כָּל־הַדָּבָ֣ר׀אֲשֶׁר־יָצָ֣א מִפִּ֗ינוּ לְקַטֵּ֞ר לִמְלֶ֣כֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם֮ וְהַסֵּֽיךְ־לָ֣הּ נְסָכִים֒ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֜ינוּ אֲנַ֤חְנוּ וַאֲבֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ מְלָכֵ֣ינוּ וְשָׂרֵ֔ינוּ בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וּבְחֻצ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַנִּֽשְׂבַּֽע־לֶ֨חֶם֙ וַנִּֽהְיֶ֣ה טוֹבִ֔ים וְרָעָ֖ה לֹ֥א רָאִֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For certainly we will do every word that has gone out from our mouth, to burn incense to [the] queen of the heavens and to pour out to her drink offerings, as we did, we and our fathers, our kings and our princes, in [the] cities of Judah and in [the] streets of Jerusalem; and we were satisfied [with] bread, and we were well, and disaster not we saw.

en.L: For we will certainly do every word that has gone out of our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her, as we did, we and our fathers, our kings and our princes, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. And we had our fill of bread, and we were well, and we saw no disaster.
en.B: Instead, we will do everything we have promised: we will burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we and our ancestors, our kings and our officials did in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Back then we had plenty of food, we were well off, and we saw no disaster.
en.R: Instead, we will do everything we promised. We will burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out wine as offerings to her. We will do what we and our ancestors, our kings and our leaders, did in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. In those days we had plenty to eat. Life was good, and nothing bad happened to us.

decisions.choice: every word that has gone out of our mouth: our vows
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of vows made to God (Numbers 30:3; Judges 11:36). Verse 25 calls these promises vows.

decisions.choice: the queen of heaven: a goddess worshiped in Judah
decisions.reason: See 7:18. The cakes, incense and drink offerings of verses 17-19 match what 7:18 describes.

decisions.choice: we had plenty ... we saw no disaster: an argument from experience
decisions.reason: They judge the gods by results: while they served the queen of heaven they prospered, so she must be the one who provided. Jeremiah answers in verses 21-23 that the disaster came because of that worship.

decisions.choice: bread: food in general
decisions.reason: As often, "bread" stands for food of every kind.

decisions.choice: the queen of heaven (all levels); princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R); wine as offerings (R)
decisions.reason: The title is kept at every level, as set for Jeremiah; Readable says what a drink offering was, as at 7:18. *Sar* follows the wording set for it.

decisions.choice: Instead (B, R); everything we have promised
decisions.reason: The opening word sets their vow against Jeremiah's message; Balanced and Readable say what "every word from our mouth" means (m1).

source.text: וּמִן־אָ֡ז חָדַ֜לְנוּ לְקַטֵּ֨ר לִמְלֶ֧כֶת הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם וְהַסֵּֽךְ־לָ֥הּ נְסָכִ֖ים חָסַ֣רְנוּ כֹ֑ל וּבַחֶ֥רֶב וּבָרָעָ֖ב תָּֽמְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And from then we ceased to burn incense to [the] queen of the heavens and to pour out to her drink offerings, we have lacked everything, and by the sword and by the famine we have been finished.

en.L: But since we stopped burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything, and we have come to an end by the sword and by famine."
en.B: But from the time we gave up burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring drink offerings out to her, we have been in need of everything and have been wiped out by sword and famine."
en.R: But since the day we gave up burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out wine to her, we have had nothing. We have been dying in war and of famine."

decisions.choice: since we stopped: probably from the time of Josiah's reform
decisions.reason: The text does not say when they stopped. The likeliest time is King Josiah's reform, when the worship of other gods was put down (2 Kings 23:4-14). Josiah's death in battle, the rule of Egypt and then Babylon, and the fall of Jerusalem followed (2 Kings 23:29-25:21). They took these disasters as the goddess's anger.

decisions.choice: we have come to an end: the very word God used in verse 12
decisions.reason: They use the same verb as God's sentence: they agree that they are perishing, but they blame the wrong cause.

decisions.choice: the end of the people's reply
decisions.reason: The answer begun in verse 16 ends here. The next verse speaks for the women.

decisions.choice: by the sword and by famine (L); by sword and famine (B); in war and of famine (R); wine (R); speech closes
decisions.reason: The pair follows the wording set for Jeremiah, and Readable says "wine" for the drink offerings, as at 7:18.

source.text: וְכִֽי־אֲנַ֤חְנוּ מְקַטְּרִים֙ לִמְלֶ֣כֶת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּלְהַסֵּ֥ךְ לָ֖הּ נְסָכִ֑ים הֲמִֽבַּלְעֲדֵ֣י אֲנָשֵׁ֗ינוּ עָשִׂ֨ינוּ לָ֤הּ כַּוָּנִים֙ לְהַ֣עֲצִבָ֔ה וְהַסֵּ֥ךְ לָ֖הּ נְסָכִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And when we [were] burning incense to [the] queen of the heavens and pouring out to her drink offerings, [was it] without our husbands [that] we made for her cakes to portray her and poured out to her drink offerings?

en.L: "And when we were burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, was it without our husbands that we made cakes for her to portray her, and poured out drink offerings to her?"
en.B: "And when we were burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring drink offerings out to her, did we make cakes bearing her image and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands' consent?"
en.R: The women added, "Our husbands knew all about it when we were burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out wine to her. We did not make cakes that showed her image or pour out wine to her without their approval."

decisions.choice: our husbands: the women now speak
decisions.reason: "Our husbands" shows that the speakers are the women of verse 15. The Hebrew does not say so in words, and the verb forms are those used for a mixed group. Some ancient translations add words naming the women as the speakers (from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: without our husbands: the husbands had consented, so the vows stood
decisions.reason: Under the law a wife's vow stood if her husband heard of it and said nothing; he could cancel it on the day he heard (Numbers 30:7-16). The women claim their husbands' approval, so the vows were binding and their husbands shared in them.

decisions.choice: to portray her: cakes shaped like the goddess or stamped with her image
decisions.reason: The verb means to shape or fashion. The cakes may have been made in the goddess's form, or marked with her image or symbol, such as a star. Some take the verb in another sense, "to worship her" or "to please her". The exact sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: cakes: offering cakes for the goddess
decisions.reason: See 7:18. The word is borrowed from the language of Mesopotamia and is used only here and in 7:18.

decisions.choice: consent (B); The women added; approval; a statement for the question (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "without our husbands" means. Readable names the speakers (m1) and gives the answer the question expects, as a statement.

decisions.choice: to portray her (L); bearing her image (B); that showed her image (R)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the uncertain sense open between a shaped cake and a stamped one (m3). A new quotation opens and closes here for the new speakers.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ אֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֑ם עַל־הַגְּבָרִ֤ים וְעַל־הַנָּשִׁים֙ וְעַל־כָּל־הָעָ֔ם הָעֹנִ֥ים אֹת֛וֹ דָּבָ֖ר לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeremiah to all the people, to the men and to the women and to all the people who [were] answering him [a] word, saying:

en.L: Then Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men and to the women and to all the people who had given him [this] answer, saying:
en.B: Then Jeremiah spoke to all the people, the men and the women, all the people who had given him this answer. He said:
en.R: Then Jeremiah spoke to all the people, men and women, who had answered him this way. He said:

decisions.choice: who had answered him: the reply of verses 16-19
decisions.reason: Jeremiah answers the whole crowd, men and women together, who had given that reply.

decisions.choice: [this] (L); this answer (B); this way (R); He said (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they answered him "a word"; the levels make clear it was the answer just given.

records.literal_gloss: Not the incense which you burned in [the] cities of Judah and in [the] streets of Jerusalem, you and your fathers, your kings and your princes and [the] people of the land, them did remember Yahweh, and it came up on his heart?

en.L: "The incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, you and your fathers, your kings and your princes, and the people of the land, did not {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} remember them, and did it not come up into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind?
en.B: "The incense you burned in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, you and your ancestors, your kings and your officials, and the people of the land: has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} not remembered it, and has it not come into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind?
en.R: "You burned incense in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. You did it, and so did your ancestors, your kings, your leaders and the people of the land. Do you think {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not remember it? He kept it all in mind.

decisions.choice: the incense ... you and your fathers, your kings and your princes: Jeremiah turns their own words back on them
decisions.reason: He repeats the list from verse 17. The worship they credit for their good years is the very thing the LORD remembered against them.

decisions.choice: come up into his mind: be thought of, called to mind
decisions.reason: The idiom means to come to mind (3:16; 7:31). Here it means God took note of it.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the ordinary citizens of Judah
decisions.reason: The phrase names the free landholding people, set beside kings and officials (1:18; 34:19).

decisions.choice: them: the offerings, or those who made them
alternatives: did the LORD not remember them (the people)?
decisions.reason: The word "them" may refer to the many offerings of incense, or to the people just listed. Either way God did not overlook it.

decisions.choice: it (B, R); Readable as statements and a question; princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "it" for the incense (m4). Readable states the facts first and then asks the question, answering it in a short sentence. A new quotation opens for Jeremiah's reply, which runs to the end of verse 23.

source.text: וְלֹֽא־יוּכַל֩ יְהוָ֨ה ע֜וֹד לָשֵׂ֗את מִפְּנֵי֙ רֹ֣עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֥י הַתּוֹעֵבֹ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֑ם וַתְּהִ֣י אַ֠רְצְכֶם לְחָרְבָּ֨ה וּלְשַׁמָּ֧ה וְלִקְלָלָ֛ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵׁ֖ב כְּהַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And not was able Yahweh any longer to bear because of [the] evil of your deeds, because of the abominations which you did; and became your land a ruin and a horror and a curse, without inhabitant, as the day this.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} could no longer bear [it], because of the evil of your deeds, because of the abominations that you committed; so your land has become a ruin and a horror and a curse, without inhabitant, as [it is] this day.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} could no longer bear your evil deeds and the detestable things you did, so your land became a ruin, a horror and a curse, with no one living in it, as it is today.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} could not put up any longer with your evil deeds and the disgusting things you did. That is why your land has become a ruin, a horror and a curse, with no one living there, as it is today.

decisions.choice: bear: endure, put up with
decisions.reason: The verb means to carry a load. God's patience had a limit, and their deeds reached it (Isaiah 1:14).

decisions.choice: abominations: things loathsome to God
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, the word names above all the worship of other gods.

decisions.choice: a ruin, a horror and a curse: the land destroyed, appalling and used in curses
decisions.reason: As in 25:18 and verse 12.

decisions.choice: ruin, horror, curse (all levels); abominations (L), detestable things (B), disgusting things (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for these lists in Jeremiah, and for *to'evah* as in verse 4.

source.text: מִפְּנֵי֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר קִטַּרְתֶּ֜ם וַאֲשֶׁ֧ר חֲטָאתֶ֣ם לַיהוָ֗ה וְלֹ֤א שְׁמַעְתֶּם֙ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֔ה וּבְתֹרָת֧וֹ וּבְחֻקֹּתָ֛יו וּבְעֵדְוֺתָ֖יו לֹ֣א הֲלַכְתֶּ֑ם עַל־כֵּ֞ן קָרָ֥את אֶתְכֶ֛ם הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Because that you burned incense and that you sinned against Yahweh, and not you listened to [the] voice of Yahweh, and in his law and in his statutes and in his testimonies not you walked, therefore has met you the disaster this, as the day this.

en.L: Because you burned incense and because you sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and did not listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and did not walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instruction and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} testimonies, therefore this disaster has come upon you, as [it is] this day."
en.B: It is because you burned incense and sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and would not listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or live by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instruction, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decrees, that this disaster has come upon you, as it has today."
en.R: This disaster has happened to you, as you can see today, because you burned incense and sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You did not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You did not follow {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws or {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instructions."

decisions.choice: because you burned incense: the true cause of the disaster
decisions.reason: Jeremiah answers "since we stopped" (verse 18): the disaster came because they burned incense, not because they stopped.

decisions.choice: listen to the voice of the LORD: obey him
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to do what they say.

decisions.choice: instruction, statutes and testimonies: the whole of God's law
decisions.reason: Three words for the law stand together, as in Deuteronomy 4:45 and 6:17, to say that they kept none of it.

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B), teaching (R); statutes (L, B), laws (R); testimonies (L), decrees (B), instructions (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for these terms (Isaiah; Numbers to Ruth).

decisions.choice: the disaster first, then the reasons; speech closes
decisions.reason: Readable states the result first and then the causes in short sentences. Jeremiah's reply, opened in verse 21, closes here.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֔ם וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־הַנָּשִׁ֑ים שִׁמְעוּ֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה כָּל־יְהוּדָ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeremiah to all the people and to all the women: hear [the] word of Yahweh, all Judah who [are] in [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women, "Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all Judah who [are] in the land of Egypt.
en.B: Then Jeremiah said to all the people and all the women, "Hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all you of Judah who are in the land of Egypt.
en.R: Jeremiah spoke again to all the people, including all the women. He said, "Listen to the message of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all you people from Judah who live in Egypt.

decisions.choice: and to all the women: the women addressed in particular
decisions.reason: They spoke last (verse 19), and the vows are chiefly theirs (verse 25).

decisions.choice: all Judah: all the people of Judah in Egypt
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, the name of the nation stands for its people in Egypt.

decisions.choice: Hear (L, B), Listen (R); all Judah (L), all you of Judah (B), all you people from Judah (R); the speech opens
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the address to the people plain. Jeremiah's words run to the end of the chapter; within them, words he quotes take single quotation marks.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָֽה־צְבָאוֹת֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לֵאמֹ֗ר אַתֶּ֨ם וּנְשֵׁיכֶ֜ם וַתְּדַבֵּ֣רְנָה בְּפִיכֶם֮ וּבִידֵיכֶ֣ם מִלֵּאתֶ֣ם׀לֵאמֹר֒ עָשֹׂ֨ה נַעֲשֶׂ֜ה אֶת־נְדָרֵ֗ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָדַ֨רְנוּ֙ לְקַטֵּר֙ לִמְלֶ֣כֶת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וּלְהַסֵּ֥ךְ לָ֖הּ נְסָכִ֑ים הָקֵ֤ים תָּקִ֨ימְנָה֙ אֶת־נִדְרֵיכֶ֔ם וְעָשֹׂ֥ה תַעֲשֶׂ֖ינָה אֶת־נִדְרֵיכֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel, saying: you and your wives, and you have spoken with your mouth and with your hands you have fulfilled, saying, certainly we will do our vows which we vowed, to burn incense to [the] queen of the heavens and to pour out to her drink offerings. Certainly confirm your vows, and certainly do your vows!

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled [it] with your hands, saying, 'We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to pour out drink offerings to her.' Surely confirm your vows, and surely perform your vows!
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: You and your wives have said it with your mouths and carried it out with your hands: 'We will certainly keep the vows we made, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.' Go ahead, then: keep your vows! Carry out your vows!
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives said you would do it, and you have done it. You said, 'We will surely keep our vows to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out wine to her.' All right, then, keep your vows! Do what you vowed!

decisions.choice: you and your wives: with verbs in the feminine
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "you and your wives", but the verbs that follow are feminine, as if spoken to women only. The Greek translation reads "you women" (from general knowledge). The Hebrew is followed; either way the women are chiefly in view.

decisions.choice: surely confirm your vows: a bitter permission
decisions.reason: The commands are ironic: God gives them up to the choice they have made, and its results (compare Ezekiel 20:39; Amos 4:4). Each verb is doubled for force.

decisions.choice: vows: promises to a god that must be paid
decisions.reason: A vow, once spoken, had to be kept (Deuteronomy 23:22-24; Numbers 30:3). The women insist that their vows bind them.

decisions.choice: Go ahead, then (B); All right, then (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add a few words so that the commands are heard as ironic (m2).

decisions.choice: perform (L), keep (B, R); vows
decisions.reason: The levels use the ordinary words for keeping a vow.

source.text: לָכֵן֙ שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֔ה כָּל־יְהוּדָ֕ה הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הִנְנִ֨י נִשְׁבַּ֜עְתִּי בִּשְׁמִ֤י הַגָּדוֹל֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אִם־יִהְיֶה֩ ע֨וֹד שְׁמִ֜י נִקְרָ֣א׀בְּפִ֣י׀כָּל־אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֹמֵ֛ר חַי־אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore hear [the] word of Yahweh, all Judah who dwell in [the] land of Egypt: look, I have sworn by my name, the great, says Yahweh, if will be again my name called in [the] mouth of any man of Judah saying, [as] lives [the] Lord Yahweh, in all [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: Therefore hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all Judah who dwell in the land of Egypt: Look, I have sworn by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great name, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will no longer be called on in the mouth of any {{gender:person|man}} of Judah, saying, '[As] the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} lives,' in all the land of Egypt.
en.B: Therefore hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all you of Judah who live in the land of Egypt: I swear by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great name, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that in all the land of Egypt {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name will never again be invoked by anyone from Judah who says, 'As surely as the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} lives.'
en.R: So listen to the message of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all you people from Judah who live in Egypt. I swear by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own great name, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that no one from Judah anywhere in Egypt will ever again call on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name in an oath and say, 'As surely as the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} lives.'

decisions.choice: if my name will be called on again: an oath meaning "it will never be"
decisions.reason: In a Hebrew oath, "if it happens" means "it will surely not happen" (1 Samuel 3:14).

decisions.choice: I have sworn by my great name: God binds himself by his own name
decisions.reason: There is no one greater for God to swear by, so he swears by himself (22:5; 49:13; Genesis 22:16; Isaiah 45:23).

decisions.choice: my name will no longer be called on: no one left in Egypt to swear by the LORD
decisions.reason: The people of Judah in Egypt will perish (verse 27), and the LORD's name will no longer be heard on their lips there. They have chosen another goddess; now they lose the God whose name they still swore by.

decisions.choice: As the Lord GOD lives: the common form of an oath
decisions.reason: People swore by the life of the LORD to bind themselves to the truth (4:2; 5:2; 12:16).

decisions.choice: [As] the Lord GOD lives (L); As surely as the Lord GOD lives (B, R); invoked (B), call on in an oath (R)
decisions.reason: "Lord GOD" follows the wording set for Adonai with the divine name, and "As surely as" follows 16:14.

decisions.choice: person, with "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Any man of Judah" means anyone of Judah, women included.

source.text: הִנְנִ֨י שֹׁקֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם לְרָעָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א לְטוֹבָ֑ה וְתַמּוּ֩ כָל־אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֛יִם בַּחֶ֥רֶב וּבָרָעָ֖ב עַד־כְּלוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, I [am] watching over them for harm and not for good, and will be finished every man of Judah who [is] in [the] land of Egypt by the sword and by the famine until their being finished.

en.L: Look, I am watching over them for harm and not for good, and every {{gender:person|man}} of Judah who is in the land of Egypt will come to an end by the sword and by famine, until they are finished.
en.B: I am keeping watch over them for harm and not for good. All the people of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will perish by sword and famine until they are wiped out.
en.R: I am watching over them to bring disaster, not to do them good. All the people from Judah who are in Egypt will die in war or of famine until they are all gone.

decisions.choice: watching: the word of the almond-tree vision (1:12)
decisions.reason: God said he was "watching over my word to do it" (1:12), and later that as he had watched over his people to uproot them, he would watch over them to build and to plant (31:28). Here the watching is for harm.

decisions.choice: for harm and not for good
decisions.reason: The same words are used of Jerusalem in 21:10 and 39:16 (compare Amos 9:4).

decisions.choice: come to an end ... until they are finished
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, the verb means to perish completely.

decisions.choice: watching (L, R), keeping watch (B)
decisions.reason: The same wording as 1:12, so that the reader can hear the echo (m1).

decisions.choice: person, with "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in verse 26.

source.text: וּפְלִיטֵ֨י חֶ֜רֶב יְשֻׁב֨וּן מִן־אֶ֧רֶץ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָ֖ה מְתֵ֣י מִסְפָּ֑ר וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כָּל־שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֗ה הַבָּאִ֤ים לְאֶֽרֶץ־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לָג֣וּר שָׁ֔ם דְּבַר־מִ֥י יָק֖וּם מִמֶּ֥נִּי וּמֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And escapees of [the] sword will return from [the] land of Egypt [to the] land of Judah, men of number; and will know all [the] remnant of Judah who came to [the] land of Egypt to sojourn there whose word will stand, from me or from them.

en.L: And those who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number; and all the remnant of Judah who came to the land of Egypt to sojourn there will know whose word will stand, {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} or theirs.
en.B: Those who escape the sword and return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah will be very few. Then all the remnant of Judah who came to the land of Egypt to live there will know whose word comes true, {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} or theirs.
en.R: Only a few will escape death and return from Egypt to the land of Judah. Then all the people left from Judah who came to live in Egypt will know whose word comes true, {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} or theirs.

decisions.choice: men of number: few, easily counted
decisions.reason: The phrase means so few they can be counted (Genesis 34:30; Deuteronomy 4:27). It explains "except fugitives" in verse 14.

decisions.choice: stand: be fulfilled, prove true
decisions.reason: A word that stands is one that comes true and is not overturned (Isaiah 40:8).

decisions.choice: whose word, mine or theirs: God's word against the people's vow
decisions.reason: The people vowed to do "every word that has gone out of our mouth" (verse 17). Events will show whose word holds.

decisions.choice: comes true (B, R); very few (B); Only a few (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "stand" means (m2) and what "men of number" means (m1).

source.text: וְזֹאת־לָכֶ֤ם הָאוֹת֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־פֹקֵ֥ד אֲנִ֛י עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בַּמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה לְמַ֨עַן֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּ כִּי֩ ק֨וֹם יָק֧וּמוּ דְבָרַ֛י עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם לְרָעָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And this [will be] for you the sign, declaration of Yahweh, that visiting I [am] on you in the place this, so that you may know that certainly will stand my words against you for harm.

en.L: And this [will be] the sign to you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that I am going to punish you in this place, so that you may know that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words against you will surely stand, for harm:
en.B: This will be the sign to you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that I will punish you in this place, so that you may know that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words of harm against you will certainly come true:
en.R: Here is the sign that I will punish you in this place, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It will show you that what I have said about bringing disaster on you will surely come true.

decisions.choice: the sign: an event that confirms God's word
decisions.reason: A sign is a visible event that proves a message true (1 Samuel 2:34; Isaiah 7:14). Verse 30 names it.

decisions.choice: punish: the verb "visit" used of judgment
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: will surely stand: the verb doubled for certainty
decisions.reason: The repeated verb answers verse 28: God's words will stand.

decisions.choice: declares (L, B), says (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *ne'um YHWH*.

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִ֣י נֹ֠תֵן אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֨ה חָפְרַ֤ע מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בְּיַ֣ד אֹֽיְבָ֔יו וּבְיַ֖ד מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשׁ֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֜תִּי אֶת־צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֗ה בְּיַ֨ד נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֧ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל אֹיְב֖וֹ וּמְבַקֵּ֥שׁ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: look, I [am] giving Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into [the] hand of his enemies and into [the] hand of [those] seeking his life, as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into [the] hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy and [one] seeking his life.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am giving Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, who sought his life."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am going to hand Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies, to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, his enemy, who wanted to kill him."
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I will hand Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies who want to kill him. I will do this just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to his enemy Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, who wanted to kill him."

decisions.choice: Pharaoh Hophra: the king of Egypt in Jeremiah's last years
decisions.reason: Hophra (Apries, reigned about 589-570 BC) sent an army that briefly drew the Babylonians away from Jerusalem (37:5-7). He lost his throne in a revolt led by his general Amasis and was later killed (from general knowledge). The refugees trusted Egypt to protect them, but its king would fall like Zedekiah.

decisions.choice: as I gave Zedekiah: the fate of Judah's last king
decisions.reason: Zedekiah was captured, his sons killed before his eyes, and he was blinded and taken to Babylon (39:5-7; 52:9-11).

decisions.choice: those who seek his life: those who want to kill him
decisions.reason: As in 19:7 and 21:7.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the spelling the Hebrew uses here for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
decisions.reason: Jeremiah usually spells the name this way; it is the same king.

decisions.choice: hand ... over to (B, R); want to kill him (B, R); speech closes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "into the hand of" and "seek his life". Jeremiah's words, opened in verse 24, close here.
